subject: Post-call recap: model fit & tool-calling evals for FinData
messages:

Subject: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals for FinData

Alex,

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood so we stay aligned.

1) What we heard
- Primary use: structured extraction from earnings reports and call transcripts (entity normalization, numeric extraction, tables -> JSON).
- SLOs: high schema compliance (>=99% ingestable), handle long context (~6k tokens), and low synchronous latency for UI flows.

2) Recommended starting models
- redwood-14b-optimized — best balance of quality and throughput for structured outputs.
- redwood-owl-7b — cost-efficient for high-volume batch scoring (lower token cost).

3) Early benchmark notes (attached)
- Schema compliance failures observed: ~12% on function-calling outputs (missing required fields, wrong types, occasionally truncated arrays).
- Retry behavior: naive retries increase duplicate downstream tool invocations (we recommend idempotency keys + backoff).

Attachments: findata-benchmark-summary.csv, findata-prompt-sets.json
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinDataEval

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to run a focused eval (5k examples) covering: JSON schema validation, function-calling idempotency, retry/backoff patterns, and prompt-set robustness. Target: reduce schema failures to <2%.
- Meeting to review results & demo eval harness: Tue 2026-03-24 10:00 AM PT (proposed).

Question: would you prefer Redwood run the eval on your sample dataset (preferred) or for us to run on anonymized public examples first?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals for FinData

Sean / Alex — looping in a few technical notes from our evals team based on the attached benchmark and the prompt sets Alex shared during the call.

Summary of findings (from a 1k-sample pilot)
- Schema failures (~12%): mostly due to missing required fields (company/ticker) and type mismatches in numeric fields where the model emitted strings or formatted numbers with commas.
- Truncation in nested arrays: when the extracted "quarters" list is long (>6 entries) we see partial arrays or dropped objects.
- Function-calling: correct in intent ~85% of the time but the JSON returned often omitted optional-but-needed keys leading to downstream ingestion errors.

Suggested mitigations
- Model choice: redwood-14b-optimized with the following inference config: temperature 0.0, max_tokens tuned per output, and structured-output validators in the callback. For high-volume nightly scoring: redwood-owl-7b with post-hoc schema validation pipeline.
- Prompt engineering: enforce explicit field-level instructions + examples in the prompt set (we've attached updated prompt variants in findata-prompt-sets.json).
- Retries & idempotency: add an idempotency key on tool-side calls, and implement exponential backoff with jitter (do not blindly re-run any side-effecting tool call more than once).
- Eval harness: we recommend a structured-output eval that validates against a strict JSON schema and counts: missing fields, type mismatches, extra fields, and array truncation. This gives a clear "schema compliance" metric to track in Redwood Console.

Sample target JSON schema (for evaluator):
{"type": "object", "properties": {"company": {"type": "string"}, "ticker": {"type": "string"}, "revenue": {"type": "number"}, "quarters": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"q": {"type": "string"}, "value": {"type": "number"}}}}, "required": ["company", "ticker", "revenue"]}

Attachments: updated prompt variants (findata-prompt-sets.json). We'll run the 5k structured-output eval once dataset access is confirmed.

Let us know if you want us to include quantized model variants (4-bit) in the eval matrix — they reduce cost but may impact numeric formatting.

— Marissa
Product / Applied ML
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement. 10 AM PT on Tue 3/24 works on our side; I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and the Drive links.

Short answers:
- Ballpark cost: redwood-14b-optimized ≈ $0.015 per 1k prompt+completion tokens (estimate for baseline config). redwood-owl-7b ≈ $0.006 per 1k tokens for batch scoring — we'll include precise estimates in the follow-up deck for procurement.
- Data handling: Redwood can run the eval in a private project space with a 30-day retention policy and access-limited to the eval team; if you require an on-prem/private deployment we can scope Redwood Private (separate contract). We'll add a short data handling addendum for procurement to review.

Action items

- Marissa: run 5k structured-output eval once dataset access is confirmed; include quantized variants in the matrix if FinData wants cost/quality comparison.
- Alex / Procurement: confirm dataset transfer method (secure share preferred) and whether PII will be redacted.

I'll attach the invite and the Eval plan after this note.
